statement: Assessment for U033: the ranking question cannot be settled from the literature, but the two available patterns both argue against simple redundancy. Aggregate orderings are demonstrably slice-dependent in this exact corpus style, since a hybrid that wins overall loses to BM25 on multihop queries, so a version-level slice can plausibly reorder systems that an aggregate metric ranks identically. And the one point-in-time system with published numbers achieves 1.7% temporal leakage without reaching comparable answer accuracy, showing that a temporal metric captures failures that accuracy does not. The expected pattern is therefore partial overlap rather than identity: version-level metrics should correlate with accuracy but rank at least some system pairs differently, with the discordance concentrated on non-latest-gold queries. Because no work compares version-contamination rankings with accuracy rankings directly, U033 stays open on the specifics and is now the explicit target of plan E004, revised to add a redundancy and variance-decomposition component alongside the rank-agreement test.

evidence.quote: improves answer accuracy from 66.7% to 78.9% over hybrid RAG while reducing temporal evidence leakage from 10.8% to 1.7% and hallucination from 17.3% to 7.9%
